parts.title: Campus Conversation: Looking for a Job on Campus
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and an advisor at the campus career center.
Man
Hi there. Can I ask you a few questions?
Woman
Of course. Come in and sit down. What do you need?
Man
Thanks. I'm looking for a part-time job here on campus. I want to earn some money for my books and my phone bill.
Woman
Good. We have a lot of student jobs. How many hours can you work each week?
Man
About ten hours. My classes are mostly in the morning, so I'm free in the afternoons.
Woman

Ten hours is perfect. Most student jobs are between eight and fifteen hours a week. Let me see... The campus library needs help in the afternoons. You would put books back on the shelves and help students at the front desk.
Man
The library? That sounds nice. It's quiet, and I like books.
Woman
There is also a job at the sports center. You would clean the equipment and check student ID cards at the door. That job pays a little more, but it starts at six in the morning.
Man
Six in the morning? Hmm... I'm really not a morning person.
Woman
I understand. So the library is a better choice for you. To apply, you need to fill out an online form and upload a resume.
Man
A resume? I've never written one. I don't really know how.
Woman
That's no problem. We have a free resume workshop every Wednesday at three o'clock, right here in this office. We show you step by step.
Man
Really? That's great. I'll come this Wednesday.
Woman
Good. Bring a list of your past jobs and your volunteer work. Then you can finish your resume in one hour.
Man
OK. Thank you so much. This was really helpful.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Do We Need Sleep?
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a psychology class.
Professor
Good morning, everyone. I see some of you are yawning. That's perfect, because today's topic is sleep. Why do we need sleep?
Professor
Most adults need about seven to nine hours of sleep every night. Teenagers need even more, about eight to ten hours. But many college students sleep only five or six hours.
Professor

So what does sleep do for us? The first important job is memory. During the day, you learn many new things. At night, while you sleep, your brain organizes this new information and saves it. So if you study and then sleep well, you will remember more.
Professor

The second job is repair. While you sleep, your body fixes small problems in your muscles. Your body also makes things that help you fight sickness. People who sleep too little often get colds more easily.
Professor

Sleep happens in stages. In deep sleep, your body rests and repairs itself. In another stage, called REM sleep, your eyes move quickly, and this is when most dreams happen. REM means Rapid Eye Movement. Your brain goes through these stages four or five times every night.
Professor

Now, here's something interesting. A lot of students stay up all night before an exam. They think it helps. Actually, it usually hurts. Without sleep, it's hard to focus, and you forget what you studied.
Professor
So, here is my advice: try to go to bed at the same time every night, and put your phone away thirty minutes before bed. The light from the screen tells your brain it's still daytime.
Professor
For next class, please keep a sleep diary. Write down when you go to bed and when you wake up, every day this week.
